title: SSO + Audit-log Cutover: dependency simulation matrix, canary sequencing, and escalation plan
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Plan and track phased cutover for customer SSO (SAML/OIDC) and tenant-scoped audit-log retention across Hosted/Dedicated/Private deployments. Deliverables: a dependency simulation matrix, deterministic canary sequencing for 3-region rollouts, automated smoke validations for audit integrity, rollback triggers, and a documented escalation path for customer support and oncall. The goal is a reproducible cutover playbook that minimizes downtime and ensures auditability for SOC2/ISO audits.
acceptance_criteria: Simulation matrix covers all permutations of SSO provider types, tenant state (fresh vs migrated), and deployment modes (hosted/dedicated/private)
Canary plan demonstrates <5% error amplification across routed requests when toggling auth flows in a test tenant
Automated validation runbooks verify audit-log completeness (sequence numbers, timestamps, KMS-encryption metadata) for 14-day retention window in a synthetic workload
Rollback criteria are codified and tested in 2 dry-run exercises without customer-visible failures
Escalation contact list and playbooks (support → oncall infra → security) are reachable and acknowledged by stakeholders
milestone_sequence: M1: Dependency mapping and simulation matrix (owner: PM)
M2: Small-scale canary tooling and feature flag wiring (owner: ENG)
M3: Audit validation hooks and KV-checker tooling (owner: ENG)
M4: Cross-team dry-run (support, infra, security, PM) in staging with synthetic tenants
M5: Customer pilot cutover with rollback window and telemetry monitoring
M6: Full rollout and post-cutover compliance verification
simulation_plan: Generate 6 synthetic tenant states: new, legacy-SSO, legacy-no-SSO, partial-claims, nested-groups, delegated-auth
Run matrix of provider types: Okta, AzureAD, Ping, Generic SAML, Generic OIDC across regions us-east1/us-west1/eu-central1
Inject network partitions and region failovers to validate audit-log forwarding and local retention semantics
Capture metrics: auth success rate, token exchange latency, audit-log write latency, sequence gaps, encryption header presence
Export results to console compliance dashboard and attach CSV output to ticket
canary_and_rollout: Phase 1 canary: 2 internal tenants in us-east1, run 48h synthetic traffic
Phase 2 canary: 5 pilot customers across two regions, increase to 72h with real traffic shadowing
Decision gates: if auth failure rate >0.5% or audit sequence gaps >0 detected, trigger rollback immediately
Rollout cadence: region-by-region with 24h stabilization windows; automated pause on anomaly via SLO ranger rules
rollback_triggers: Auth degradation: 0.5% sustained failure for 15 minutes
Audit inconsistency: missing sequence numbers or >1 second out-of-order events for 5 minutes
KMS errors: >3% of audit-log writes fail with encryption error
Unrecoverable latency: median token exchange latency >1s for 30 minutes
escalation_path: Tier 1 Support → read-only mitigation (disable new SSO flows) and paging to oncall
Oncall Infra → roll back feature-flag at routing layer and validate audit replayability
Security Eng → investigate KMS/crypto anomalies and coordinate with cust-security contact
PM → customer comms: templated notification and timeline to rollback completion
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Legacy tenants with custom SAML attributes break mapping — Mitigation: attribute normalization layer + test harness
Risk: Audit-log spikes overwhelm retention pipeline — Mitigation: temporary throttles and backpressure-aware batcher
Risk: Region-specific KMS policies block encryption — Mitigation: preflight KMS policy checks and fallback key rotation plan
Risk: Operator error during canary sequencing — Mitigation: gated playbook, one-button rollback script, and required cross-team signoff
